pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 13.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION STRATEGIES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.2: Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you identify the key points while reading a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the key points in a passage
2. create mental images of the characters, places and events in the text
3. appreciate the role of reading in lifelong learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 13.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION STRATEGIES
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 13.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION STRATEGIES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the key points in a passage

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the key points in a passage. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the key points in a passage.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the key points in a passage. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create mental images of the characters, places and events in the text

What this means
In this part you learn to create mental images of the characters, places and events in the text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create mental images of the characters, places and events in the text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create mental images of the characters, places and events in the text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of reading in lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of reading in lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of reading in lifelong learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of reading in lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the key points in a passage)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies to a partner. (skill: create mental images of the characters, places and events in the text)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of reading in lifelong learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the key points in a passage.
3. Practise this skill: create mental images of the characters, places and events in the text.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of reading in lifelong learning.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you identify the key points while reading a text?
2. Which words can bring out the five senses in a text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension strategies means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the key points in a passage.
5. Be able to: create mental images of the characters, places and events in the text.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
